Raymond III Count of Tripoli was a notable noble of the Crusader states in the twelfth century. He was born around 1140 to Raymond II Count of Tripoli and his wife Hodierna of Jerusalem. His father died when Raymond was still a child and his mother acted as regent until he came of age. He inherited the County of Tripoli in 1152 after the death of his father. His early years were marked by efforts to consolidate power amid rivalries with neighboring Muslim states and with the Knights Templar who held significant influence in the region.

*Early Life and Background*

During his youth Raymond received education typical for a noble of his status. He learned martial skills Latin and the customs of the Frankish courts. He also developed ties with the Kingdom of Jerusalem through marriage alliances. In 1160 he married Eschiva of Bures a daughter of the lord of Galilee which strengthened his connections to the northern Crusader territories. The marriage produced several children including his successor Raymond IV.

*Rule as Count*

Raymond's rule was characterized by a delicate balance between warfare and diplomacy. He fought against the forces of Nur ad Din and later Saladin seeking to protect Tripoli from Muslim incursions. At the same time he negotiated treaties with Muslim leaders to secure trade routes and to obtain tribute. He also dealt with internal challenges such as the rising power of the Knights Templar who had built a formidable fortress at Tortosa and who sometimes contested his authority. Raymond supported the Third Crusade by providing troops and supplies to the crusading armies that passed through his lands. He also participated in the siege of Acre in 1189 where his contingent fought alongside King Guy of Lusignan and other Crusader leaders.

*Later Years and Death*

In the late 1180s Raymond faced increasing pressure from Saladin who had united much of Syria and Egypt under his rule. After the disastrous Battle of Hattin in 1187 Raymond retreated to Tripoli where he attempted to organize a defense. Despite his efforts the city fell to Saladin's forces in 1189 after a prolonged siege. Raymond was captured and held for a time before being released under terms that required him to relinquish certain claims. He spent his final years in relative obscurity living in exile or in reduced circumstances. Raymond III died around 1190 marking the end of an era for the County of Tripoli which subsequently fell under direct Muslim control.
